title: strength import
description: Result of `stride strength import <file|->` — strength workouts as Strava's MCP connector returns them (a list of workout objects, or one), each decoded on its own, stored in strength_logs against its activity as the text the connector wrote, and parsed into strength_sets before the command returns, so `stride strength` shows them without an analyze. A stored log takes precedence over the activity's description for that activity, and re-importing an activity replaces its log. `imported` and `skipped` together hold one entry per workout in the input, in input order within each list, and every set left out of a workout is a `dropped` entry on it: nothing in the input is left out silently. A skipped workout or a dropped set is not an error: the command exits 0 and names the reason, and only unreadable input, or input that is not a JSON object or list, fails the command.

imported.description: One entry per stored workout. `rows` counts the stored set rows (consecutive sets of one exercise at the same reps and weight fold into one row); `sets` counts the sets those rows hold; `dropped` lists the workout's sets that were left out; `zeroed` lists its bodyweight sets whose recorded weight was not counted.

set.description: the set's 1-based position in the workout's exercise_sets

exercise.description: the set's exercise name, "" when it had none

reason.description: no_exercise_name: the set names no exercise. no_reps: no rep count, timed (duration-only) sets included. bad_reps: a rep count that is not a positive whole number ("8-10", "0"). unknown_weight_unit: a weight whose value names no kg/lb/lbs unit ("44 stone", a bare "20"). bad_weight: a kg/lb weight whose number does not parse ("20,5 kg") or is negative. A set with no weight at all is kept at 0 kg, not dropped.

zeroed.description: Bodyweight sets (push up, pull up, dip, plank, ... matched by exercise name, case, spacing, hyphens and a trailing plural ignored) kept with their sets and reps at 0 kg although the log recorded a nonzero weight (the connector's log can carry the athlete's own mass on a bodyweight move). The stored log keeps the recorded weight; only the derived set rows read 0 kg.

set.description: the set's 1-based position in the workout's exercise_sets

recorded.description: the weight as the log wrote it, e.g. "79.4 kg"

skipped.description: One entry per workout left unstored. `activity_id` is the input's value as given, a string because a skipped id need not be numeric ("" when the workout carried none or it could not be read).

reason.description: undecodable_workout: the element is not a workout object the import can read (not an object, or exercise_sets or a set field of the wrong type). bad_activity_id: absent, null, not a whole number, or not positive. duplicate_activity: an earlier workout in the same input was already stored for this activity; only a stored workout claims its activity, so one skipped for another reason does not. unknown_activity: no activity with that id in the database (sync first). not_strength: the activity is not in the strength family, the only family strength sets are counted for. no_sets: exercise_sets is empty. no_usable_sets: every set was left out; `dropped` says why for each.

dropped.description: the sets left out, populated for no_usable_sets and empty otherwise; same shape and reasons as imported[].dropped
